items.title: Field-general formative plan with unresolved venue

manuscript.title: Interruptible dashboards for shift handovers
manuscript.abstract: A synthetic pilot compares two dashboard layouts during twelve simulated shift handovers and reports lower task-completion time for the interruptible layout.
manuscript.methods: Twelve volunteers completed both layouts in counterbalanced order. The planned analysis compares paired completion times and records navigation errors. No venue has been selected.
manuscript.results: Median completion time was 84 seconds for the interruptible layout and 96 seconds for the comparison layout. Individual observations and the analysis script are retained.
manuscript.limitations: The pilot is small, uses a simulated task, and cannot establish workplace effectiveness.
manuscript.data_availability: Synthetic row-level data and analysis code are available in the study package.

items.author_intent: Plan a cautious empirical article without inventing a target venue or expanding the study into a field trial.
items.review_task: Identify the target-aware evidence and limitation checks that the outline should reserve; do not draft results or infer venue rules.

items.title: Causal overclaim under an exact synthetic profile

manuscript.title: Notification batching eliminates decision fatigue
manuscript.abstract: A synthetic workplace study states that notification batching eliminates decision fatigue and improves accuracy.
manuscript.methods: Forty workers were assigned by alternating enrollment order, not random allocation, to immediate or batched notifications. Analysts fit an unadjusted group comparison after viewing the outcome distributions.
manuscript.results: The batching group made 7.2 errors on average and the immediate group made 8.0. The confidence interval for the difference includes zero; the manuscript nevertheless describes a definitive causal effect.
manuscript.limitations: The draft mentions one organization but does not discuss allocation bias, analytic flexibility, or imprecision.
manuscript.data_availability: De-identified synthetic summary data are included; row-level records are not available.

items.author_intent: Preserve the observational workplace comparison; the author is open to recalibrating claims or a feasible re-analysis but has not authorized new data collection.
items.review_task: Perform a paper-visible internal evaluation of material weaknesses and feasible remedies while keeping venue fit separate from scientific validity.

items.title: Venue-aligned article with a separable validity defect

manuscript.title: Accessible chart annotations in screen-reader workflows
manuscript.abstract: A synthetic empirical article evaluates two annotation formats for screen-reader users and is within the declared journal scope.
manuscript.methods: Twenty-four participants completed both formats. The paper reports only the fastest trial per participant and does not disclose that selection rule until the discussion.
manuscript.results: The selected fastest trials favor structured annotations. A sensitivity analysis using all trials is not reported, although all synthetic trials remain available.
manuscript.limitations: The discussion describes recruitment constraints but treats the fastest-trial estimate as representative of routine use.
manuscript.data_availability: All synthetic trial records are available for re-analysis.

items.author_intent: Retain the accessibility contribution and declared venue; the author permits re-analysis but not a change to the research question.
items.review_task: Write an editorial-level review that distinguishes venue alignment from the validity consequence of outcome selection.

items.title: Reporting overlay with recoverable flow omissions

manuscript.title: Search interfaces for multilingual evidence synthesis
manuscript.abstract: A synthetic systematic review compares search-interface features across 31 studies.
manuscript.methods: Two screeners used a documented query and retained the screening log. The manuscript omits full-text exclusion counts and reasons even though the log contains them.
manuscript.results: Thirty-one studies are summarized without inventing effect estimates. Study-level extraction tables are internally consistent.
manuscript.limitations: Language coverage and database selection are disclosed. The missing flow information is not discussed.
manuscript.data_availability: The synthetic query, extraction table, and screening log are available.

items.author_intent: Complete the report from retained records; collecting new studies or changing inclusion criteria requires an explicit author choice.
items.review_task: Assess methodological and reporting weaknesses, distinguishing a minimum documentation remedy from stronger work that would require new screening.

items.title: Interdisciplinary criteria that must remain parallel

manuscript.title: Transparent early-warning models across classroom contexts
manuscript.abstract: A synthetic learning-analytics article reports an interpretable risk model deployed in three classroom settings.
manuscript.methods: Feature definitions and code are documented, but classroom implementation differs by site and one site omits the support intervention offered after an alert.
manuscript.results: Discrimination is similar across sites. The paper pools sites for its main conclusion and provides no site-specific calibration table.
manuscript.limitations: The authors note institutional variation but do not connect it to intervention delivery or interpretation of pooled performance.
manuscript.data_availability: Synthetic code and aggregate site tables are available; student-level data are withheld.

items.author_intent: Keep the interdisciplinary contribution. The author will add feasible site-level reporting but will not imply that computing transparency resolves educational-context concerns.
items.review_task: Keep conflicting computing-transparency and education-context criteria parallel and give useful, evidence-bounded remedies for any material finding.

items.title: Adversarial clean control

manuscript.title: Replicated keyboard layouts for one-handed text entry
manuscript.abstract: A synthetic preregistered crossover study compares two keyboard layouts and reports an imprecise, non-definitive difference in entry speed.
manuscript.methods: The preregistered paired analysis was run on all 60 participants. Allocation order, exclusions, measures, code, and stopping rule match the retained protocol.
manuscript.results: The estimated difference is 1.1 words per minute with a 95% interval from -0.8 to 3.0. The manuscript states that the data are compatible with small effects in either direction and makes no superiority claim.
manuscript.limitations: The authors identify short follow-up, laboratory tasks, and uncertain generalization to long-form use.
manuscript.data_availability: Synthetic row-level data, protocol, and analysis code are available.

items.author_intent: Publish a calibrated null-compatible result without adding an unsupported superiority claim or unnecessary new-data demand.
items.review_task: Adversarially search for a genuine Critical or Major weakness; return no material finding when the supplied record does not support one.
